items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Because you were mentioning a Hamilton College alumnus, Al Vollmer, he doesn’t like bebop but he likes Charlie Parker.

ctx.x: Yeah that’s right in the little circle there. So you felt compelled to find out more about him?

Well if the angle we’re heading towards is why Bird, you know why does Charlie Parker become such a focal point in my career, I think I can explain that to you and I think it’s two parts. One is my discovering that he’s a good way to push jazz. Because you were mentioning a Hamilton College alumnus, Al Vollmer, he doesn’t like bebop but he likes Charlie Parker.

items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: Phil Schaap used to try to trick him. But you couldn’t.

ctx.x: Well we got Fred Staton at 102, and of course Larry Lucie lived to be 101. And so that there, and then many of them got to be 90. I mean Johnny Williams was the original bass player who was in the band for 25 years. He was 90 and then he died. And Laurel Watson who was one of the singers, she was just about 90. Certainly, oh when Clyde discovered in his church in Newark the New Eden Baptist Church in Newark, he discovered Princess White, who her real name was Princess, her real name was Princess White Durrah. And…
